nodes.label: DEC-001 Trunk-based versioning on main
nodes.rationale: One branch to trust satisfies the 'latest approved version' requirement; lower overhead than GitFlow for a solo founder with no long-lived develop branch to drift; tags plus changelog give named, auditable milestones without ceremony. GitFlow and main-only/commit-direct were both considered and rejected. Amended by DEC-004 (2026-07-30): push cadence changed from session-end-only to continuous; everything else in the decision stands.

nodes.label: Waypoint (Startup Project)
nodes.rationale: The repository is the single source of truth: product definition, decisions, knowledge, architecture, and eventually code all live in one versioned repo pushed to GitHub, so any human or agent opening it sees the current truth.

nodes.label: Trunk-Based Development
nodes.rationale: Chosen so main is one branch to trust that always shows the latest approved version. Lower overhead than GitFlow for a solo founder (no long-lived develop branch to drift); main-only direct commits rejected because short-lived branches give a cheap review point before work becomes approved. Branches must stay short-lived (hours to days) or they defeat the model.

nodes.label: Semantic Versioning
nodes.rationale: Tags plus changelog give named, auditable milestones without ceremony. MAJOR = breaking/directional change, MINOR = new capability or phase, PATCH = fixes; pre-1.0 (v0.x.y) signals the project is still forming.

nodes.label: Keep a Changelog Format
nodes.rationale: Human-readable history of approved versions; every tag gets an entry written when the tag is created, not after.

nodes.label: Conventional Commits
nodes.rationale: Structured commit messages (type(scope): summary) keep history legible; types are feat, fix, docs, chore, refactor, test.

nodes.label: Agent Attribution Footer
nodes.rationale: Multiple tools and machines may touch the repo, so every commit carries computer, tool, version, and timestamp read from the real environment to keep history traceable; unknown values are written as 'unknown', never omitted or guessed.

nodes.label: Version-Timestamp Convention
nodes.rationale: No silent undated versioned artifacts: every doc, deck, script, config, or report carries a visible Version-Timestamp header; vault notes use the 'updated:' YAML frontmatter field for the same purpose.

nodes.label: Obsidian Vault as Project Memory
nodes.source_file: vault/02-Decisions/DEC-002 Obsidian vault as project memory.md
nodes.rationale: Persistent, versioned project memory exists to prevent agent amnesia across sessions: every session starts from START-HERE plus the latest session note rather than re-reading the repo.

nodes.label: Graphify Knowledge Graph
nodes.source_file: vault/02-Decisions/DEC-003 Graphify as queryable project brain.md
nodes.rationale: Serves as the queryable project brain: task-specific context is retrieved with graphify query against graph.json instead of re-reading raw repo files, minimizing token cost.

nodes.label: Post-Commit Graph Rebuild Hook
nodes.source_file: vault/02-Decisions/DEC-003 Graphify as queryable project brain.md
nodes.rationale: Rebuilds the graph from code changes for free using AST parsing, no LLM tokens. Limitation: covers only code; doc updates remain a manual, protocol-enforced --update step at session end.

nodes.label: Token Cost Telemetry
nodes.source_file: vault/02-Decisions/DEC-003 Graphify as queryable project brain.md
nodes.rationale: Accumulates per-run token counts so the cost of maintaining and querying project memory stays visible instead of hidden.

nodes.label: Session-End Checklist
nodes.rationale: Mandatory, never skipped: write the session note, update START-HERE, rebuild the graph if docs changed, commit and push. Exists because local-only history does not count as saved and a brand-new session must be able to resume from START-HERE plus the latest session note alone.

nodes.label: Context Retrieval Order
nodes.rationale: Ordered to minimize token cost: always-loaded protocol file, then START-HERE, then a budgeted graphify query, then targeted vault notes via wikilinks, with raw file reads as last resort. Exists to prevent amnesia-driven re-reading of the whole repo.

nodes.label: Engineering Mantra (Security, Stability, Reliability, Compliance)
nodes.rationale: Applies to everything shipped: validate input, handle errors on external calls, no silent failures, no hardcoded secrets, accessibility for anything user-facing; lint and verify before claiming done.

nodes.label: GitHub Repo (mollyparty/waypoint)
nodes.rationale: Remote origin; pushing here at every milestone and session end is what makes history count as saved.

nodes.label: Your AI Running Coach (Product Concept)
nodes.rationale: Working tagline discovered in the remote GitHub README; adopted as the product concept placeholder. Full product definition (features, differentiation, business model) is deliberately deferred to a dedicated product discovery session.

nodes.label: Agent-Attribution commit footer
nodes.rationale: Values are read from the real environment (hostname, tool, version, timestamp) so history stays traceable across the multiple machines and tools that may touch the repo; unknown values are written as 'unknown' rather than omitted.

nodes.label: Engineering mantra: security, stability, reliability, compliance
nodes.norm_label: engineering mantra: security, stability, reliability, compliance

nodes.label: CLAUDE.md (Claude Code pointer file)
nodes.rationale: A symlink from CLAUDE.md to AGENTS.md was considered but rejected because core.symlinks is disabled on this machine (common on Windows without developer mode), which would store the link as an unusable plain-text path reference; a real short pointer file works identically everywhere at the cost of one nearly-empty file to keep in sync. Duplicating full agent instructions per tool was also rejected because it guarantees drift.

nodes.label: CONTRIBUTING.md (collaborator onboarding doc)
nodes.rationale: Added as the human-facing onboarding doc covering clone, git identity, tool choice, the Obsidian vault, Graphify setup, and contribution workflow, so any collaborator (including Claudio's partner) can pick the project up cold from any machine or tool.

nodes.label: DEC-004: Continuous push and cross-IDE agent files
nodes.source_file: vault/02-Decisions/DEC-004 Continuous push and cross-IDE agent files.md
nodes.rationale: Two requirements surfaced once a second collaborator (Claudio's partner) entered the picture: (1) GitHub must always reflect current work, not just work committed at session end, so a partner can pull main at any moment and see the latest; (2) the project must be fully usable from any AI coding tool on any machine, not only inside the Cursor workspace. Keeping push cadence at session-end only, and using separate tool-specific instruction files with duplicated content, were both rejected as alternatives.
nodes.norm_label: dec-004: continuous push and cross-ide agent files

nodes.label: Continuous push policy (commit and push after every meaningful unit of work)
nodes.source_file: vault/02-Decisions/DEC-004 Continuous push and cross-IDE agent files.md
nodes.rationale: Amends DEC-001's session-end-only cadence. Continuous push has an overhead cost (more, smaller commits) but directly serves the goal that a human collaborator must never be blocked waiting for a session to 'finish'; more frequent commits in history are intentional, not noise.
nodes.norm_label: continuous push policy (commit and push after every meaningful unit of work)

nodes.label: Cross-IDE / cross-tool compatibility (Cursor, Codex CLI, Claude Code, Gemini CLI, others)
nodes.rationale: One canonical AGENTS.md plus thin, non-duplicated pointer files (e.g. CLAUDE.md) avoids duplicating agent instructions per tool, which would guarantee drift; this is the maintainable version of a 'reference, don't embed' principle.
nodes.norm_label: cross-ide / cross-tool compatibility (cursor, codex cli, claude code, gemini cli, others)

nodes.label: .gitattributes line-ending normalization (eol=lf)
nodes.source_file: vault/02-Decisions/DEC-004 Continuous push and cross-IDE agent files.md
nodes.rationale: Normalizes line endings so the repo is byte-identical on Windows, macOS, and Linux, avoiding spurious diffs between collaborators on different operating systems; applied as a one-time repo-wide renormalization pass, already completed.

nodes.label: Research Playbook (research/00-RESEARCH-PLAYBOOK.md)
nodes.rationale: Operating manual for the research-to-blueprint program; any agent in any IDE runs phases to its standards.

nodes.label: Nine-phase gated research program (Phase 0 to Phase 8)
nodes.rationale: Founder brief through Business Blueprint; each phase gated on Claudio's approval, Phase 4 concept lock is the heaviest gate.
nodes.norm_label: nine-phase gated research program (phase 0 to phase 8)

nodes.label: Citation and confidence-labeling standard ([verified]/[inferred]/[assumption])
nodes.rationale: Every claim sourced and labeled; no source, no claim; assumptions never silently absorbed.

nodes.label: Phase definition-of-done gate checklist
nodes.rationale: Nine conditions including vault knowledge notes, session note, graph update, push, and Claudio's gate approval.

nodes.label: Phase 1: Market and industry research
nodes.rationale: Market landscape, TAM-SAM-SOM with methodology, industry trends, regulatory compliance.

nodes.label: Phase 2: Competitor analysis
nodes.rationale: Profiles (Runna, TrainAsONE, AI Endurance, Coopah, Joggo; adjacent Strava, Garmin, Nike Run Club, WHOOP, Apple Fitness+), feature and pricing matrices, positioning map, gap analysis.

nodes.label: Phase 3: User research
nodes.rationale: Segmentation, evidence-based personas, jobs-to-be-done, pain points mined from reviews and forums, ranked unmet needs.

nodes.label: Phase 4: Synthesis and concept lock
nodes.rationale: Opportunity, positioning, locked concept document, and the verdict on every Founder Brief hypothesis.

nodes.label: Phase 5: Product definition and MVP scope
nodes.rationale: PRD, RICE prioritization, MVP scope with the ONE core job, user journeys, stack recommendation.
nodes.norm_label: phase 5: product definition and mvp scope

nodes.label: Phase 6: Business model and go-to-market
nodes.rationale: Business Model Canvas, revenue model, directional unit economics, North Star metric, GTM plan.

nodes.label: Phase 7: HTML research dashboard on Vercel (deployment protection required)
nodes.rationale: Static HTML presenting all research; confidential pre-launch material must not deploy unprotected.
nodes.norm_label: phase 7: html research dashboard on vercel (deployment protection required)

nodes.label: Phase 8: Business Blueprint (investor deliverable)
nodes.rationale: Markdown master blueprint plus investor-facing HTML site on Vercel; the fundraising instrument.

nodes.label: Founder Brief (Claudio's vision, 2026-07-30 interview)
nodes.rationale: Founder vision captured before research; source of testable hypotheses H1 to H7.

nodes.label: Adaptive route generation (hero wedge)
nodes.rationale: Routes adapting to distance, elevation, humidity and weather, street crossings, safety, surface; coaching layers on top. The product's atomic unit is the route.

nodes.label: Problem: where to run in unfamiliar situations
nodes.rationale: Runners on vacation, travel, or unexpected scenarios do not know where to run or how to get a routine fit to their body, schedule, and needs.
nodes.norm_label: problem: where to run in unfamiliar situations

nodes.label: Target user: the committed amateur runner
nodes.rationale: Runs 3 to 5 times per week, races a few times a year (5K to marathon), wants to improve, will not pay a human coach. To be validated in Phase 3.
nodes.norm_label: target user: the committed amateur runner

nodes.label: Testable hypotheses H1 to H7
nodes.rationale: Route friction (H1), no incumbent solves constraint-based routes (H2), route wedge beats plan wedge (H3), freemium willingness to pay (H4), venture-scale market (H5), iOS-first form factor (H6), routine personalization deepens retention (H7).

nodes.label: Business intent: venture-scale, freemium subscription, seed in 12 months
nodes.rationale: MVP live with thousands of active runners and a seed round closed or in motion within 12 months; the blueprint is the fundraising instrument.
nodes.norm_label: business intent: venture-scale, freemium subscription, seed in 12 months

nodes.rationale: Built research scaffolding, ran founder interview, recorded DEC-005; key reveal was the route-generation wedge.

nodes.label: Market landscape research (running, fitness, AI coaching markets)
nodes.rationale: Market definitions, published sizing, 2025 consolidation wave, value chain, participation data for US, England, races.
nodes.norm_label: market landscape research (running, fitness, ai coaching markets)

nodes.label: Market sizing: TAM $1.3B to $2.9B, SAM 14M runners, SOM $5M to $30M ARR
nodes.rationale: Tests H5 with top-down report figures, observable-revenue cross-checks, and a bottom-up build anchored on Runna's ~90k payers at acquisition.
nodes.norm_label: market sizing: tam $1.3b to $2.9b, sam 14m runners, som $5m to $30m arr

nodes.label: Industry trends research (wearables, AI coaching, subscriptions, routing tech, running culture)
nodes.rationale: 40 verified findings; three most consequential: platform squeeze, unowned route-generation hero feature with cheap stack, Gen Z running boom.
nodes.norm_label: industry trends research (wearables, ai coaching, subscriptions, routing tech, running culture)

nodes.label: Regulatory and compliance research (location, health data, AI Act, accessibility, subscriptions)
nodes.rationale: Concrete obligations plus a 15-item MVP compliance checklist; not legal advice.
nodes.norm_label: regulatory and compliance research (location, health data, ai act, accessibility, subscriptions)

nodes.label: Finding: route-generation whitespace is real and unowned
nodes.rationale: Training apps prescribe workouts without location intelligence; routing apps plan static routes without training context; nobody generates the run itself. Enabling stack (OSM routing, free elevation and weather, on-device AI) is nearly zero marginal cost, so the moat is personalization and execution.
nodes.norm_label: finding: route-generation whitespace is real and unowned

nodes.label: Finding: H5 venture-scale verdict UNCERTAIN
nodes.rationale: The wedge alone benchmarks to $5M to $30M ARR by year 5 (Runna anchor): a strong business and strategic exit, but venture scale requires an expansion story (Android, geographies, broader coaching surface).

nodes.label: Finding: platform giants commoditize generic AI coaching
nodes.rationale: Garmin Connect+ ($6.99/mo) and Apple Workout Buddy (motivational, not prescriptive) raise the bar; differentiation must be what they do not do.
nodes.norm_label: finding: platform giants commoditize generic ai coaching

nodes.label: Risk: Garmin Connect Developer Program paused to new applicants
nodes.rationale: HealthKit remains fully open (validates iOS-first) but Garmin integration is a launch risk.
nodes.norm_label: risk: garmin connect developer program paused to new applicants

nodes.label: Guardrail: location privacy is day-one architecture (privacy zones, private-by-default)
nodes.rationale: Generated routes anchored at home reveal home address (Strava heatmap precedent); precise geolocation is sensitive data across GDPR and ~19 of 20 US state laws; EU AI Act Article 50 transparency applies 2026-08-02.
nodes.norm_label: guardrail: location privacy is day-one architecture (privacy zones, private-by-default)
